title: ai_vendor_vetting_criteria
primary_keyword: AI adoption in a large company
claim: Enterprise AI tools fail in marketing not from bad outputs, but from unmanaged legal liability and data privacy exposure in the supply chain.
hook: 90% of AI risk sits in your vendor contract.

evidence.detail: A 4-point procurement sanity check for enterprise marketing technology evaluation: training data indemnity, data retention window, downstream model ownership, and liability cap alignment.

reel_script.voiceover: Generative tools look simple at the desk. But scaling AI adoption in a large company breaks at legal sign-off.

reel_script.onscreen: Where is your brand data retained?
reel_script.voiceover: Most enterprise teams check output quality. Almost none check if input prompts train public base models by default.

reel_script.onscreen: If they fail one point, block the license.
reel_script.voiceover: If an AI software vendor cannot sign all four conditions in writing, do not deploy them across your communications team.
AI governance is not a brake on marketing execution. It is the boundary that allows enterprise scale without legal rollback.

caption:
90% of AI risk sits in your vendor contract.

Successful AI adoption in a large company is rarely stopped by prompt quality. It gets killed six months later when legal reviews the enterprise software agreement.

Most B2B communications leads test tools for speed and output style. Meanwhile, the software vendor retains prompt inputs to train public base models, exposing confidential product specifications to public indexing.

If your martech vendor cannot grant full copyright indemnity and guarantee zero data retention for training, you are taking on unmanaged corporate risk.

Governance is not the enemy of speed. Clear boundaries are what allow large organizations to deploy tools safely.

Send this to whoever is evaluating AI software vendors for your team this quarter.
